People who make mistakes in public often feel embarrassed for days or even weeks afterwards.
Some cultures are much more tolerant of mistakes than others, particularly in the workplace.
Largely because we're so focused on our own behaviour that we find it hard to imagine others aren't.
s.a: Soru "Why does that happen?"; boşluğun altında "So we assume everyone else is paying as much attention to us as we are?" özeti var. Boşlukta sebep, kendimize aşırı odaklanmamız olmalı. "Largely because we're so focused on our own behaviour" hem sebebi veriyor hem özete bağlanıyor. Katılımcı sayısı ve kültür farkı cevap değil.

s.q:
Tourist: - Is it safe to drink the water from the mountain streams here?
Guide: - ----
Tourist: - But it looks so clear. How could it be harmful?
Guide: - Clear water can still contain bacteria and parasites that you can't see.
o: The streams are fed by melting snow from the peaks in spring.
Yes, it's perfectly safe; you can drink as much as you like.
There is a small café at the top where you can buy food and drinks.
I wouldn't risk it. Boil or filter it first.
Most visitors come here in summer, when the paths are dry and the views from the top are at their best.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "But it looks so clear. How could it be harmful?" var: "But" bir itiraz, demek ki rehber suyun riskli olduğunu söylemiş. "I wouldn't risk it. Boil or filter it first" bu uyarıyı veriyor. "Yes, it's perfectly safe" itirazla kopuyor; kafe ve kar suyu şıkları soruya cevap değil.

s.q:
Doctor: - How long have you been having these headaches?
Patient: - ----
Doctor: - I see. Have you changed anything in your routine recently, such as your working hours?
Patient: - Actually, yes. I've been spending much longer in front of a computer screen.
o: I've never really had a headache before in my whole life.
My mother and my sister also suffer from headaches occasionally.
I usually take a painkiller and lie down in a dark room for an hour.
The pharmacy near my house is open until ten o'clock tonight.
For about three weeks now, mostly in the late afternoon.
s.a: Doktor 'How long' diye soruyor: boşlukta süre bildiren bir cevap olmalı. 'For about three weeks now' süreyi veriyor ve doktorun 'recently' diye son değişiklikleri sormasına zemin hazırlıyor. Daha önce hiç baş ağrısı çekmediğini söyleyen şık süre sorusunu cevaplamıyor.

s.q:
Student: - I don't understand why the Romans abandoned some of their provinces.
Historian: - ----
Student: - So holding on to them simply cost more than they were worth?
Historian: - In many cases, yes, especially when the empire was under pressure elsewhere.
o: The Romans built thousands of kilometres of roads across their territory to move their armies quickly.
Latin remained the language of education in Europe for centuries.
Some provinces were famous for their wine and olive oil.
Defending distant borders took more soldiers and money than the empire could often afford.
Historians still disagree about the exact date when the empire began.
s.a: Soru bazı eyaletlerin neden terk edildiği; boşluğun altında "So holding on to them simply cost more than they were worth?" özeti var. Boşlukta bir maliyet sebebi olmalı. Uzak sınırları savunmanın karşılanamayacak kadar asker ve para gerektirdiğini söyleyen şık özete bağlanıyor. Yollar ve şarap şıkları cevap değil.

s.q:
Tom: - Have you seen my keys anywhere?
Sara: - ----
Tom: - Oh yes, I remember now. I put them there when I came in.
Sara: - You should always leave them in the same place.
o: Aren't they on the table next to the front door?
I lost my keys last week, too.
Let's take the bus instead of the car today.
You can borrow my spare set if you're going out this evening.
I think the door's already locked.
s.a: Soru anahtarların nerede olduğu; boşluğun altında "Oh yes, I remember now. I put them there" var. "there" referansının karşılığı boşlukta bir yer olmalı. "Aren't they on the table next to the front door?" bu yeri veriyor. Yedek anahtar ve kilitli kapı şıklarında "there" sözcüğünün gideceği bir yer yok.

s.q:
Interviewer: - Many people assume that creativity declines with age. Is there any truth in that?
Psychologist: - ----
Interviewer: - So older people may produce fewer ideas, but better ones?
Psychologist: - In many fields, yes. Experience helps them judge which ideas are worth pursuing.
o: Not really. With age, people come up with ideas more slowly, but their quality often improves.
Creativity is notoriously difficult to define, let alone measure.
Many famous artists, poets and composers produced their best work when they were still very young.
I'd say creativity is mainly a matter of hard work and practice.
Children are naturally creative, but school often discourages them.
s.a: Soru yaratıcılığın yaşla azalıp azalmadığı; boşluğun altında "So older people may produce fewer ideas, but better ones?" özeti var. Boşlukta hız ile nitelik ayrımı olmalı. "Not really" ile fikirlerin daha yavaş geldiğini ama niteliğin arttığını söyleyen şık özete bağlanıyor. Genç sanatçılar şıkkı özetle çelişiyor.

s.q:
Interviewer: - You've written twelve novels. Do you still find writing difficult?
Author: - ----
Interviewer: - That sounds exhausting. How do you keep going?
Author: - I remind myself that every book I've finished once felt impossible too.
o: My first novel was published when I was twenty-five.
No, it has become so easy that I can finish a book in a few weeks.
More than ever, to be honest. Each new book seems to demand that I learn how to write all over again.
I usually write in the mornings and read in the afternoons.
Many of my readers have asked me to write a sequel to my last book, so I've started planning one this year.
s.a: Soru "Do you still find writing difficult?"; boşluğun altında "That sounds exhausting" var. Boşlukta yazmanın hâlâ, hatta daha da zor olduğu söylenmeli. "More than ever" ile her kitapta yazmayı yeniden öğrenmek gerektiğini söyleyen şık iki satıra bağlanıyor. "it has become so easy" yorumu ters çeviriyor.

s.q: (I) Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money, but not everyone is affected equally. (II) People on fixed incomes, such as pensioners, tend to suffer most, as their incomes do not rise with prices. (III) Borrowers, by contrast, may benefit, since the real value of their debts falls over time. (IV) Central banks in most developed countries aim to keep inflation at around two per cent a year. (V) Savers who keep their money in accounts with low interest rates also see the real value of their savings decline.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu enflasyon, limit herkesi eşit etkilememesi. II sabit gelirlileri, III borçluları, V tasarruf sahiplerini anlatarak etkilenen grupları sıralıyor. IV merkez bankalarının enflasyon hedefine geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama "kim nasıl etkileniyor" limitini tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) Dogs were probably the first animals to be domesticated by humans. (II) Early hunters may have found that wolves which stayed near their camps were useful for hunting and protection. (III) Over thousands of generations, these animals gradually became tamer and more dependent on people. (IV) Cats are popular pets in many countries because they are easy to look after. (V) Today, there are hundreds of dog breeds, each developed for a particular purpose.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu köpeğin evcilleştirilmesi. II kurtların kamplara yaklaşmasını, III "these animals" ile evcilleşmeyi, V bugünkü köpek ırklarını veriyor. IV kedilerin neden sevildiğine geçiyor; kahraman değiştiği için konu dışı. Çıkarınca III ile V kronolojik olarak bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Many migratory birds travel thousands of kilometres between their breeding and wintering grounds every year. (II) Remarkably, they often return to exactly the same nesting site. (III) Scientists believe that they find their way by combining several cues, including the position of the sun and the stars. (IV) Some species also appear to be able to sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a kind of compass. (V) The Arctic tern, one of these long-distance travellers, can live for more than thirty years.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu göçmen kuşlar; II'den itibaren limit, aynı yuvaya nasıl geri döndükleri. III ve IV güneş, yıldızlar ve manyetik alan gibi yön bulma ipuçlarını veriyor. V kutup sumrusunun ömrüne geçiyor; "one of these long-distance travellers" referansı tutsa da yön bulma limitinin dışında.

s.q: (I) Trees planted along city streets can lower local temperatures by several degrees in summer. (II) Their leaves provide shade and release water vapour, which cools the surrounding air. (III) As a result, neighbourhoods with plenty of trees tend to be noticeably cooler than those with few. (IV) Some tree species, such as the ginkgo, have existed in much the same form for more than two hundred million years. (V) For this reason, many city councils now regard tree planting as a cheap way of protecting residents from heatwaves.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu sokak ağaçları, limit kentte sıcaklığı düşürmesi. II nasıl serinlettiğini, III "As a result" ile sonucunu veriyor. IV bazı ağaç türlerinin ne kadar eski olduğuna geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. Çıkarınca V'teki "For this reason" III'teki serinliğe bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) The printing press, developed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1450, made it possible to produce books in large numbers for the first time. (II) Before this, every copy of a book had to be written out by hand, which took months. (III) Within fifty years, millions of books had been printed across Europe. (IV) The resulting spread of ideas played a major part in the religious and scientific changes of the following centuries. (V) Gutenberg himself made little money from his invention, having lost control of his workshop in a legal dispute.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu matbaa, limit kitapların çok sayıda basılabilmesi ve bunun etkileri. II öncesini, III hızlı yayılışı, IV "The resulting spread of ideas" ile sonucu veriyor. V mucidin icadından para kazanamamasına geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama etki limitini tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) The printing press, developed in Europe in the fifteenth century, dramatically reduced the cost of producing books. (II) As a result, ideas could spread far more quickly and widely than before. (III) Some historians argue that it played a key role in the Reformation and later in the Scientific Revolution. (IV) Paper had been invented in China many centuries earlier, during the Han dynasty. (V) By making texts identical and widely available, printing also helped to standardise languages and spelling.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu matbaa, limit etkileri: kitap ucuzladı, II "As a result" ile fikirler yayıldı, III büyük değişimlerdeki rolü, V "also" ile dilin standartlaşması. IV kâğıdın çok önce Çin'de icat edilişine geçiyor; hem kahraman hem dönem farklı, etki limitinin dışında.

s.q: (I) Clinical trials of new drugs are usually divided into several phases, each designed to answer different questions. (II) In the first phase, a small number of healthy volunteers receive the drug so that its safety can be assessed. (III) Volunteers in some countries are paid for their time, while in others they receive only their travel expenses. (IV) Later phases involve hundreds or thousands of patients and compare the new drug with existing treatments. (V) Only if a drug passes all of these stages can it be approved for general use.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu klinik denemeler, limit evreleri. II ilk evreyi, IV "Later phases" ile sonraki evreleri, V "all of these stages" ile onay şartını veriyor. III gönüllülere yapılan ödemeye geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. Çıkarınca II ile IV doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight. (II) Most species hunt at night, finding their way in the dark by means of echolocation. (III) They emit high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes that bounce back from objects around them. (IV) Dolphins use a similar system to find fish in dark or cloudy water. (V) This allows bats to detect an insect as small as a mosquito while flying at full speed.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu yarasalar; II ve III limitin yankıyla yön bulma olduğunu gösteriyor. IV yunusların benzer sistemine geçiyor; kahraman değişiyor. Çıkarınca V'teki "This allows bats" III'te anlatılan yankı sistemine doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest in the world. (II) It covers parts of nine countries in South America. (III) Football is the most popular sport in Brazil. (IV) The forest is home to an enormous variety of plants and animals, many of which have not yet been studied. (V) It also plays an important role in regulating the climate of the whole planet.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu Amazon yağmur ormanı. II yerini, IV canlı çeşitliliğini, V iklimdeki rolünü veriyor. III Brezilya'da futbolun popülerliğine geçiyor; konu dışı. Çıkarınca IV'teki "The forest" II'de anlatılan ormana doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Volcanic eruptions can have effects far beyond the area surrounding the volcano. (II) When Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted in 1815, it released enormous amounts of ash and gas into the atmosphere. (III) These particles reflected sunlight back into space, causing global temperatures to fall. (IV) As a result, 1816 became known in Europe and North America as 'the year without a summer', with crop failures and food shortages. (V) Indonesia has more active volcanoes than almost any other country in the world.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu yanardağ püskürmeleri, limit uzak bölgelere etkisi. II–IV Tambora örneğini sebep-sonuç zinciriyle veriyor: kül ve gaz, "These particles" ile güneş ışığının yansıması, "As a result" ile yazsız yıl. V Endonezya'daki yanardağ sayısına geçiyor; limit dışı.

s.q: (I) Volcanic eruptions are not all alike: some release slow rivers of lava, while others are violent explosions. (II) What decides the style of an eruption is mainly the amount of silica in the magma. (III) Magma that is low in silica is runny, so the gases dissolved in it escape easily and the lava flows out quietly. (IV) Magma rich in silica, by contrast, is thick and sticky, and it traps the gases until the pressure becomes great enough to blow the volcano apart. (V) Over time, the ash that falls on the surrounding land produces some of the most fertile soils in the world.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu püskürmelerin farklılığı: sakin lav akıntısı mı, patlama mı. II bunu belirleyenin silika olduğunu, III ve IV "by contrast" ile az ve çok silikalı magmayı karşılaştırıyor. V külün toprağı verimli kılmasına geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama "püskürme türünü ne belirler" limitini tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) The Silk Road was not a single route but a network of trade paths connecting China with the Mediterranean. (II) Along these routes, merchants exchanged goods such as silk, spices and precious metals. (III) Silk is produced by the larvae of moths that feed on mulberry leaves. (IV) Equally important, however, was the exchange of ideas, religions and technologies that travelled with the traders. (V) Buddhism, for example, spread from India to China partly through contacts made along these routes.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu İpek Yolu, limit ise ticaret ağı olarak işlevi: mal ve fikir alışverişi. III konu içinde ama ipeğin nasıl üretildiğini anlatarak limitin dışına çıkıyor. Çıkarınca II'deki mal alışverişi, IV'teki "Equally important, however" ile fikir alışverişine doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Recycling paper saves trees, water and energy. (II) Each tonne of recycled paper saves a significant amount of water compared with making new paper. (III) Paper was first made in China about two thousand years ago. (IV) However, paper fibres become shorter every time they are recycled, so paper cannot be recycled forever. (V) For this reason, new fibres must regularly be added to keep the quality of the paper high.
o: I
II
III

s.q: Tea was first drunk in China thousands of years ago, possibly as a medicine. ---- From there, it spread along trade routes to Japan, Central Asia and eventually Europe. s.q: Many people assume that deserts are lifeless places. ---- Cacti store water in their thick stems, and many desert animals are active only at night, when temperatures are lower.
